task_only_assessment.structures_and_quantifiers: Any unital, possibly noncommutative ring; any left module; one linear endomorphism. Each actual set {T^n x:n in N} is finite, with no finite-generation, finite-length or uniform orbit bound. N uses n>=0; P uses a positive integral period. Naturality ranges over arbitrary same-ring intertwiners to any other qualifying module.
task_only_assessment.independent_route: The finite orbit repeats at n<n+p. Put k=np and y=T^k x. Since k>=n, y is periodic; since k is a multiple of p, T^n(x-y)=0. N and P are submodules and N intersection P is zero. Unique decompositions force linearity, the direct-product/direct-sum equivalence, kernel/range/idempotence and naturality. The restriction of T to P is injective by the zero intersection and surjective using T^(p-1)y.
boundary_checks: n=0 gives k=0,y=x and nil component zero; p=1 causes no exception.
The zero module and zero ring are allowed; all maps/equivalences reduce correctly.
Noncommutativity is harmless: only powers of the same R-linear endomorphism commute; no scalar polynomial factorization is assumed.
No global nilpotence exponent or global positive period is needed.
Intertwiners may be zero, noninjective or nonsurjective.

reference_review.note: Actual orbit finiteness is distinguished from finite span. Submodule addition uses m+n and pq; scalar closure includes additive inverses. If a vector is nilpotent and p-periodic, np>=n and T^(np)x=x=0, including n=0.

Pigeonhole produces a positive period of a tail. k=np simultaneously lies in the tail and is a period multiple. Both membership conditions and uniqueness of the periodic component are proved, rather than presumed.

Addition and scalar multiplication preserve valid decompositions, so unique components define a genuinely linear map. The stated inverse of the product equivalence, kernel, image and idempotence follow. Any map satisfying the two membership conditions is already pointwise unique.

The restriction has a separately justified inverse existence. Intertwining extends to every power, preserves both submodules, and decomposition uniqueness gives the naturality equation in the correct direction.

invalid_path_witness_review.argument: The left shift on the F2 direct sum is locally nilpotent since each vector has finite support. It is surjective by shifting support right, so every iterated image equals M although P=0. T^m e_m=e_0 proves no uniform nilpotence exponent. This witness satisfies the actual task premise.

A vector occupies finitely many finite cycle blocks, hence has a common positive period. For any proposed positive global q, a basis vector in the q+1 block is not fixed by T^q. Thus P=M while no global finite period exists; the actual premise holds.

Multiplication by 2 on Q has one-dimensional orbit span but infinite nonzero orbit, and N=P=0. It intentionally does not satisfy the original finite-orbit premise and is correctly used only against replacing that premise by finite orbit-span dimension.

The swap over F2 has finite orbits but division by 2 is unavailable. The separate statement that averaging, when defined, targets fixed vectors rather than all periodic vectors is correct (e.g. a nontrivial finite-order operator over Q).

task_only_assessment.structures_and_quantifiers: P is only a poset and may be empty. A,B,C,M are complete lattices; maps are jointly monotone in all actual parameters/variables. alpha is a lower adjoint to gamma and satisfies exact one-step intertwining. No omega continuity, finite height, alpha invertibility, Galois insertion or meet preservation is supplied.
task_only_assessment.independent_route: Define each least solution as the meet of all prefixed points. This yields parameter monotonicity. Two-block Bekić elimination follows by comparing the assembled fixed point with every joint prefixed point; repeated application and coordinate order isomorphisms cover all three-variable partitions and orders. alpha(sigma) is Psi-fixed, giving tau<=alpha(sigma). Conversely alpha(gamma(tau))<=tau and intertwining yield Phi(gamma(tau))<=gamma(tau); least-prefixed comparison and adjunction yield alpha(sigma)<=tau.
boundary_checks: Empty P is vacuous and does not require a chosen parameter.
A complete lattice is nonempty through top/bottom; singleton factors and all singleton factors work.
One block is the simultaneous lfp; two blocks use Bekić; three singleton blocks use it twice. Coordinate changes cover either elimination orientation and all six permutations.
The proof does not require any increasing omega chain to converge to a fixed point.
alpha need not be injective or surjective. Its right adjoint is used through the counit and inequality conversion.

reference_review.note: The meet of prefixed points is a fixed point by two opposite inequalities. Its universal prefixed-point comparison implies pointwise monotonicity in the update and hence monotonicity in p. No continuity or complete structure on P is introduced.
The inner lfp function is proved monotone before substitution. The assembled pair is fixed and below every joint prefixed pair, proving true leastness rather than only solving the equations.
Two applications cover nested three-block elimination. Swapping and regrouping actual coordinates is an order isomorphism, so uniqueness of the least joint solution identifies every final result.

Both transport inequalities are justified. In particular the reverse direction uses alpha gamma(t)<=t, monotonicity of U, the adjunction twice and prefixed-point minimality; no inverse for alpha is assumed.

invalid_path_witness_review.argument: For the specified powerset map, each finite bottom iteration is an initial segment of N, their omega union is N, T(N)=N union {omega}, and every fixed point must contain all naturals and omega. It is monotone and embeds into the task with singleton other blocks/parameter and identity adjunction.

On the two-point chain, f(x,y)=y and g(x,y)=1 are jointly monotone. Freezing the other input at bottom gives (0,1), which is not fixed. Correct substitution gives the least solution (1,1). A singleton third factor and identity adjunction complete the task structure.

The constant-top alpha commutes with identity updates but sends their bottom lfp to top. It has no right adjoint because the adjunction at x=y=0 would be false iff true. It deliberately fails the original adjunction and correctly refutes only the weakened assertion that a general monotone semiconjugacy suffices.
Identity on the two-point chain has two fixed points and only bottom is least, demonstrating why checking equations alone is insufficient.

location.note: critical_errors[0] says to prove applicable order continuity before identifying the omega-iteration supremum with the least fixed point.

findings.finding: Order continuity is sufficient but not necessary. A valid argument may prove directly that the omega supremum is fixed, or prove finite stabilization, and then compare iterates with every prefixed point. The current broad acceptance policy protects these routes, so this is a wording defect rather than a false main target or a pilot blocker.
findings.mathematical_witness: On P(N union {w}), let T(U)={w} when N is a subset of U and T(U)=empty otherwise. T is monotone and T(empty)=empty, so the omega iteration from bottom is constantly empty and is the lfp. T is not omega-order-continuous: for U_n={0,...,n-1}, all T(U_n)=empty whereas T(union U_n)={w}. Thus proving global/applicable order continuity is not a necessary obligation for a correct lfp identification.
findings.recommended_fix: Replace the entry by: Identify the supremum of the omega iterations with the least fixed point without proving that this supremum is a fixed point (for example via an applicable continuity theorem); monotonicity alone does not suffice. Keep acceptance of direct stabilization and alternative complete proofs explicit.

task_only_assessment.structures_and_quantifiers: Arbitrary metric X,Y with only Y complete, dense D, an arbitrary set I carrying a proper filter, and a shared finite nonnegative Lipschitz constant. The source is the actual metric completion. The conclusions concern the whole family along the original filter, every compact subset, and every moving input along the same filter.
task_only_assessment.independent_route: Extend each Lipschitz map uniquely to the completion. The completion image of D is dense, so a three-term distance estimate transfers Cauchy behavior to every completion point. Complete Y gives unique pointwise limits; a limit of the common Lipschitz inequalities retains exactly K. Dense-data uniqueness follows from Hausdorff uniqueness and continuity. Finite compact covers give full-filter compact uniform convergence; a direct Lipschitz error estimate handles moving inputs without any compact range assumption.
boundary_checks: If X is empty, D and its completion are empty and all assertions reduce to the unique empty map. Y may then be empty.
If X is nonempty, propriety of the filter implies I is nonempty, and the given f_i implies Y is nonempty; no extra inhabitance assumption is needed.
K=0 is covered by epsilon/[4(K+1)] without division by K; the Lean type permits K=0.
The empty compact set is vacuous; singleton and arbitrary nonempty compact sets use finite covers.
A proper principal filter need not see values outside its support; no relative compactness of the full indexed value set is inferred.
No cofinal sequence is assumed for the arbitrary filter; sequences are only used as a permissible construction of individual completion extensions.
The range of a filter-convergent moving input need not lie in a compact set; the direct estimate avoids that unsupported assertion.

reference_review.note: Sequence approximations in a metric completion construct the individual extensions independently of the indexing filter. Common Lipschitz bounds prove Cauchy images, independence of approximation and preservation of K. Density and separation give uniqueness.

Density of iota(D) and epsilon/[4(K+1)] control both spatial errors strictly below epsilon/4. A common filter set from the Cauchy observation controls the middle error below epsilon/2. Mapped proper filters stay proper, so completeness gives actual values in Y. Empty domains are explicitly addressed.

Both pointwise limits use the same proper filter, so continuity of distance and the closed real inequality preserve K. Agreement on dense observed data and continuity proves uniqueness of the recovery.

Compactness is used only to obtain finitely many centers. The finite intersection of corresponding convergence sets is a filter member; it controls all points of C simultaneously. No exchange of infinite pointwise and eventual quantifiers occurs.
The synchronized limit is bounded by the spatial Lipschitz error plus the fixed-point convergence error, both tending to zero. No common compact range for u is required.

invalid_path_witness_review.argument: The tents max(0,1-|x-n|) are 1-Lipschitz and eventually vanish at every fixed x. Their height at n stays 1, so no global uniform convergence; pairs of well-separated late tents have supremum difference 1, so no global uniform Cauchy property. R/Q density and completeness assumptions hold.

The rational inclusion is 1-Lipschitz with constant-index data along any given proper filter, and Q completes to R. This witnesses that new input points in the completion are real and cannot be identified with original rational input points.

Finite subsets of an uncountable set form a directed set with proper tail filter. A countable sequence of finite subsets misses some singleton tail because its union is countable. Singleton domain/codomain data satisfy every analytical assumption, while no cofinal sequence exists.

Under the principal filter at index 0, constants f_n(*)=n have mapped filter equal to the principal filter at 0, hence are Cauchy and convergent. All maps are 0-Lipschitz, but the full value set is unbounded in R. The text correctly rejects only an unverified compactness theorem application, while allowing legitimate other compactness routes.
